name: leo-stack
description: Stack opinado sobre la suite de mattpocock/skills: solo lo que tiene sentido junto con el pipeline AFK, más la obra original que no tiene equivalente upstream. Núcleo: host-orchestrator, motor de pipeline PRD host-nativo. Adaptado en parte de mattpocock/skills (MIT).

plugins.name: host-orchestrator
plugins.description: v4.1.0: control de effort por rol y por issue (`role_efforts` → `args.efforts`, `args.issueEfforts`) + tres recortes de costo derivados de la autopsia de 4 corridas reales (2026-07-27) que midió tokens por rol en los transcripts de agentes: el costo escala con turnos × contexto acumulado, NO con el effort (output por corrida 187k-457k vs cache read 47M-215M; apagar todo el razonamiento de los 13 reviewers ahorraría ~6%). (a) APPLIER POR TANDAS (§3.7c, `applier_chunk`, default 4): el applier único de la corrida prd0019-0722 corrió 491 turnos con el contexto creciendo de 44k a 462k → 115M de tokens leídos, 39% de esa corrida en UN agente; ahora la tanda 1 crea el worktree aislado y las siguientes hacen cd con contexto fresco, acumulando aplicadas/falladas (tanda muerta → sus fixes van a `humano`). (b) DIFF PRE-FILTRADO POR UNIDAD (§3.7b): cada reviewer hace `git diff -- <paths de su unidad>` en vez del diff integrado completo (fallback '.'), sin tocar cobertura. (c) DISCIPLINA DE CONTEXTO en implementer y applier: reporters silenciosos, tests del área mientras se itera, no releer archivos ya leídos, leer rangos (un implementer de 269 turnos costó 79M, más que los 13 reviewers juntos). Defaults de effort: scout/validator/serializer low, implementer/applier medium, resolver/particionador/reviewer/judge high — la fleet NO se recorta para ahorrar: el gate es puramente numérico y el judge no recupera falsos negativos. Host-side orchestration of the full AFK pipeline. v4.0.0 (BREAKING): the pipeline engine is now a deterministic Workflow script (`workflows/prd-pipeline.js`, launched by the new `/prd-pipeline` command) — rules run as JS code, agents only implement/measure/resolve. Gate = pure `if` over validator numbers (generic ratchet: no metric worsens vs wave baseline, no before-green test goes red, diff must touch tests; invalid measurement is NEVER success). Integration-branch policy: creates `prd/<milestone>` (or `batch/<slug>`), issue PRs target it, base merged in before each wave, run ends with ONE draft PR to base for Leo's green button. All remote mutations serialized through idempotent check-then-act serializer agents (work-identity keyed, audit-logged). Capability tiers T0-T3 instead of model names (mapping only in repo config `model_map`); the launching session is the T0 orchestrator and pins each node's tier at design time. Native review fleet phase (partition → reviewers → judge → applier → gate). Resume via Workflow journal: `resumeFromRunId` only if nothing changed by hand, fresh run always safe. Spec: docs/SPEC-v4-workflow-engine.md (grilled 2026-07-16, validated by Piloto 1 ratchet-TS 2026-07-17: 6/6 criteria, 3 resumes without duplicated mutations). REMOVED in v4.0.0: `/afk-pipeline`, `/goal` wrapping, state.json, PROGRESS.md, cc-afk env-var scaffolding (only Bash/API timeouts survive). Kept as standalone surgical tools: `/parallel-implement-wave` (2-6 issues, parallel worktree subagents) and `/merge-orchestrate` (2-7 PRs, serial intent-aware merge). Custom subagents: `parallel-implementer` (TDD vertical-slice discipline, never pushes) and `merge-resolver` (5 no-regression criteria, recommends — serializer executes). Explicit invocation only; the Workflow tool's own opt-in gate doubles the marketplace rule.
